category_mapping_requirements: Use the exact registered source ID, source version or date, verification status and verification date from the sealed baseline context.
Identify a precise article, paragraph, clause, annex, numbered section, principle or control; generic thematic locators are prohibited.
State the category-specific supported claim, relationship, mapping rationale, applicability conditions and exclusions.
Do not infer compliance, control satisfaction, legal applicability or decision authority from source registration or domain coverage.
Do not combine multiple instruments, publications or mutable collections behind one source ID.
decision_eligible_requirements: The register and approval record are APPROVED and the source record is VERIFIED.
The record identifies one stable instrument or publication with an official publisher location, exact edition or date, authority tier, authority type and applicability conditions.
The source is in force or published and is not a draft, proposal, collection page, mutable topic page, withdrawn, superseded or under development.

VERIFIED means source governance checked the publisher, title, instrument or publication identifier, version or date, publication or legal status, canonical location, authority classification and licensing boundary—not only URL reachability.
Licensed standards remain metadata- and locator-only unless separate, explicit usage rights permit storage or transmission of protected content.
A VERIFIED record may be used only within its stated authority boundary and never substitutes for assessment-time applicability or interpretation.

approval_record.authority_statement: Approved as the governed source identity, authority-classification, provenance and A–F domain-coverage register for baseline composition. Approval does not establish case-specific legal applicability, legal interpretation, compliance, control satisfaction, residual-risk acceptance or lifecycle authorization.
approval_record.change_control: Never overwrite this approved artifact. A source identity, edition, status, official location, authority classification, licensing boundary or coverage change requires a successor semantic version, source-governance verification, renewed approval, dependency revalidation and a newly sealed baseline. Existing runs remain bound to their original register version and hash.

authority_boundary: This register owns stable source identity, exact publication identity, authority tier and type, official location, edition or date, verification metadata, licensing boundary and bounded A–F coverage. It does not contain category-level clause mappings or case evidence. Category objects own exact locators, supported claims, mapping rationale, applicability and exclusions. Registration alone cannot satisfy a control, prove compliance or authorize a governance decision.

authority_tiers.meaning: Binding legislation and primary rights instruments. A source is normative only when its jurisdictional, material, actor, role and temporal applicability conditions are established for the assessed case.

Official non-binding guidance, government and intergovernmental frameworks, EU agency publications and published consensus standards. These sources support interpretation, risk management or assurance but must not be represented as legislation.
Recognized community technical guidance. These sources may support threat models, tests, examples and control design but cannot independently establish legal obligations, compliance or approval.
